findings.F1: The book loses after the signal bar, not on it: in the 690 bars where a fresh short signal was held, the position gained +0.17 % per bar (sum +1.15); in the 487 bars it was carried after the signal it lost -0.21 % per bar (sum -1.02); trades lasting 3–5 days lost -2.86 % net (79 trades) and 5–10 days lost -3.27 % (128 trades), against -1.19 % for trades of 3 days or less (366); all 617 trades were short, -1.65 % gross and -1.75 % net on average, giving a Sharpe of -0.03.
findings.F2: The short fires on every up day in the profile, including tiny ones: the share of bars with a negative forecast is 1.0 for every rise above 0 in usual moves. The smallest rises (0–0.5 usual moves) are 118 of the 225 short cases at 3 days, and they are followed by +0.77 % excess (t 0.69, 60 days), so those shorts lose. Rises of 0.5–1 usual moves are followed by -1.62 %, and rises above 1 usual move by -2.97 % (t -1.36, 24 days, strength -0.32).
findings.F3: The forecast's size does not track the rise: because the ratio is standardised against its own past 60 values, the two largest entry-forecast quartiles lost -4.28 % and -3.47 % net per trade, while the second quartile earned +0.83 %. The book bets most where the idea's own measure is not largest.
findings.F4: The give-back is much larger in deeper declines. For rises above 0.5 usual moves with a 60-day return below -30 %, the 3-day excess is -5.62 % (t -2.94, 42 cases on 17 days, strength -0.65), against -3.67 % (t -1.39, 15 days) with a 60-day return between -10 % and -30 %. Depth alone is not the effect: in the same deep declines without a sizable rise (0.5 usual moves or less) the coin returns +2.25 % (t 1.17, 33 days), which a short would lose.
findings.F5: The fade grows with the horizon. For rises above 0.5 usual moves, the excess is -2.21 % over 3 days (t -1.37, 52 days) and -4.03 % over 5 days (t -2.41, 25 cases on 14 days, strength -0.31). Rises of 0.5–1 usual moves are followed by -8.7 % over 10 days (9 cases, t -4.75). Each of these moves is 10 to 40 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade.
findings.F6: The effect lives in the profile. Outside the falling agitated market, 3-day excess after rises above 1 usual move ranges from -1.0 % to +1.0 % with no t beyond 1.8. Over 5 days, rises above 2 usual moves continue upward (+7.9 %, t 2.70, 41 cases).

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day rise measured directly in standard deviations of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger the fall in its price over the next 3 days, with small up days carrying almost none of it.
ideas.consequence: A trader would short in proportion to the day's rise in usual swings themselves, so most of the weight goes on large up days rather than on every up day.
ideas.name: raw-sized one-day rise fade

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day rise against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, and the deeper its 60-day fall, the larger the fall in its price over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size the short on a sharp up day by how deep the coin's decline already is, shorting most in the steepest declines.
ideas.name: deep-decline one-day rise fade

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day rise against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger the fall in its price over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold the short on a sharp up day for about five days, giving the slow give-back time to play out.
ideas.name: one-day rise fades over 5 days
